question: Which declaration tells the browser to use modern HTML standards?
explanation: The HTML doctype declaration places the browser in standards mode; it is not an ordinary HTML element.

question: Which attribute on the html element identifies the primary language of a page?
explanation: The lang attribute, for example lang="en", identifies the language used by the document.

question: Where should a page’s character encoding normally be declared?

options.text: In a meta element inside head
In a paragraph at the top of body
As an attribute on every text element

explanation: A meta element such as <meta charset="UTF-8"> in the head declares the document character encoding.

question: Which element supplies the text commonly shown in a browser tab?
explanation: The title element in the document head provides the page title used by browser tabs and bookmarks.

question: Which semantic element is best suited to the dominant, unique content of a page?
explanation: The main element represents the dominant content of the body and normally appears only once per page.

question: Which element is intended to group major navigation links?
explanation: The nav element marks a section whose purpose is to provide navigation links.

question: For an explicitly associated label, which value must match the input’s id?
explanation: The label for value must equal the associated input id, such as for="email" with id="email".

question: How should an informative image provide a text alternative to assistive technology?

options.text: Add a caption attribute to body
Use a meaningful alt attribute on img

explanation: A meaningful alt attribute communicates the important information conveyed by an informative image.

question: Which attribute defines the destination of a standard hyperlink?
explanation: The href attribute gives the URL or fragment destination for an anchor element.

question: When an external link opens with target="_blank", which rel values are a good explicit safety practice?
explanation: noopener prevents access to the opener window; noreferrer also suppresses referrer information.

question: Which form attribute identifies the URL that receives submitted form data?
explanation: The action attribute specifies the URL that processes a form submission.

question: Which input type gives browsers a semantic hint to validate an email address?
explanation: type="email" enables email-oriented input behavior and built-in format validation in supporting browsers.

question: Which element provides a caption for a group of related form controls inside a fieldset?
explanation: The legend element labels a fieldset and helps users understand the purpose of the grouped controls.

question: Which element creates an unordered list of items?
explanation: The ul element represents a list where item order is not inherently meaningful; its items are generally li elements.

question: In an HTML table, which element represents a header cell?
explanation: The th element marks a header cell. Scope can clarify which rows or columns it describes.

question: What does scope="col" on a table header cell communicate?

options.text: The cell is hidden from screen readers
The header applies to cells in its column

explanation: scope="col" identifies a column header relationship for assistive technologies.

question: What is the default behavior of a button element inside a form when its type is omitted?

options.text: It acts only as a link

explanation: A button associated with a form defaults to submit behavior, so type="button" should be set for non-submit actions.

question: What does the required attribute on a supported form control do?

options.text: It gives the field a default value
It hides the field until clicked
It prevents submission while the field is empty

explanation: The required attribute invokes browser constraint validation and blocks submission until a value is provided.

question: Which element can provide predefined suggestions for an input without restricting users to those choices?
explanation: A datalist supplies suggestions to an input through its list attribute, while users may still enter other values.

question: What is the purpose of the defer attribute on a classic external script?

options.text: It runs the script before parsing begins
It repeats the script after every click
It downloads in parallel and runs after parsing, in document order
It converts the script to a module

explanation: A deferred classic script downloads while HTML is parsed and executes after parsing, preserving order among deferred scripts.

question: Which selector targets every element with class="card"?
explanation: A dot followed by a class name selects elements whose class list includes that name.

question: In the same origin and cascade layer, which selector generally has greater specificity?
explanation: div.notice includes a class selector and an element selector, so it has greater specificity than a single class selector or element selector.

question: What does box-sizing: border-box change about an element’s declared width?

options.text: It excludes both padding and border from the width
It includes padding and border in the width
It forces the width to be 100%

explanation: With border-box, the declared width includes content, padding, and border; margins remain outside that width.

question: Which statement correctly distinguishes margin from padding?

options.text: Margin is outside the border; padding is between content and border
Margin is text spacing; padding is line spacing
Padding is outside the border; margin is inside it
They are aliases for the same property

explanation: Margin controls space outside an element’s border, while padding controls space between the content and border.

question: In a flex container with flex-direction: row, what does align-items: center do?

options.text: Centers items along the main horizontal axis
Centers items along the cross axis, usually vertically
Makes all items the same width

explanation: For a row flex container, the cross axis is vertical, so align-items: center aligns items vertically within the container.

question: In a row flex container, which property distributes items along the main axis?
explanation: justify-content distributes flex items along the main axis, which is horizontal when flex-direction is row.

question: Which declaration creates a grid with three equal flexible columns?
explanation: repeat(3, 1fr) defines three tracks that each take an equal share of the available grid space.

question: An element with position: fixed is normally positioned relative to which reference?
explanation: A fixed-position element is generally positioned relative to the viewport, though certain ancestor properties can establish a containing block.

question: An absolutely positioned element is usually positioned relative to what?

options.text: The nearest ancestor that establishes a containing block, often position: relative
The nearest element with display: block in every case

explanation: Absolute positioning uses its containing block, commonly established by a positioned ancestor such as one with position: relative.

question: Which statement about z-index is most accurate?

options.text: It changes the document reading order
It always works identically across all stacking contexts
It controls stacking order within the applicable stacking context
It moves an element along the x-axis

explanation: z-index affects stacking order within stacking contexts; a child cannot escape its ancestor stacking context merely by using a very large value.

question: What is 1rem typically relative to?
explanation: The rem unit is based on the computed font size of the root element, usually html.

question: What is a common purpose of max-width on a content container?

options.text: To make the element ignore padding
To force horizontal scrolling on small screens
To set a fixed minimum height
To prevent the container from growing beyond a chosen width

explanation: max-width caps the element’s width while allowing it to shrink when available space is smaller.

question: Which CSS feature conditionally applies styles at specified viewport widths?
explanation: Media queries let a stylesheet apply rules only when conditions such as viewport width match.

question: Which pseudo-class applies while a pointing device is over an element?
explanation: The :hover pseudo-class matches an element while the user designates it with a pointing device, where supported.

question: Which selector creates a stylable generated box before an element’s content?
explanation: The ::before pseudo-element creates generated content before an element’s content; the content property is generally needed for it to appear.

question: Which property primarily controls the vertical spacing between lines of text?
explanation: line-height sets the height of a line box and is commonly used to tune text line spacing.

question: Which declaration creates a smooth transition from one background color to another across an element?
explanation: linear-gradient() creates an image with a smooth progression between color stops and can be used as a background.

question: What does transition: opacity 200ms ease; specify?

options.text: A 200-millisecond easing transition for changes to opacity
A delay before the page loads

explanation: The shorthand sets the transitioned property, duration, and timing function for changes to opacity.

question: Which at-rule defines named animation stages that can be referenced by the animation property?
explanation: @keyframes defines an animation’s stages, which can then be applied to an element with animation properties.

question: Which property adds a shadow behind an element’s border box?
explanation: box-shadow draws a shadow around an element’s box; text-shadow instead applies to glyphs in text.
